lifecycle.notes: task_lifecycle.py owns every transition. The AI worker never edits this file. A task that burns through max_attempts becomes blocked instead of being retried forever.

autonomous_loop_policy.discovery_policy: Discovery is the fallback for an empty queue, not the default activity. select_task.py always prefers a concrete evidence-backed task, whatever the priority numbers say, which is why this entry deliberately carries a low priority.

tasks.title: Discover concrete, evidence-backed improvements in omp-desktop and file them as tasks

evidence.detail: Initial discovery task. The AI worker must run the project's own quality gate (npm ci; npm run typecheck; npm run lint; npm test; npm run build) plus cargo fmt/clippy/test, and only file follow-up tasks backed by a real failing check, a reproducible bug, or a measured regression. Findings must be emitted in the machine-readable AUTONOMOUS_TASKS block so import_discovery_tasks.py can add them to this queue. Never touch release/version/updater files.

execution.note: the worker session for this task had already finished

tasks.title: Investigate Terminal input, output and continuity: Observable behavior and contracts

evidence.detail: Read-only scoped investigation; do not change product files or open a PR. Choose one user journey in this area; exercise a normal transition and a boundary input using isolated synthetic data. Compare frontend behavior with its backend contract and capture expected versus observed results. On a revisit choose a different journey or investigate a previous next_hypothesis; do not repeat a generic quality gate. Use isolated synthetic data, never live sessions or credentials. Record observed findings or explicit no-change with evidence in AUTONOMOUS_RESEARCH_BEGIN/END and concrete proposals in AUTONOMOUS_TASKS_BEGIN/END. No release, updater, control or secret changes.
